Let's dive into Chapter 5: Managing Criticism and Letting Go of Self-Accusation.
You know, worry often grows from the fear of criticism—whether it’s from others, or that little voice inside our own heads. But what if you could learn to handle criticism in a way that actually helps you, instead of weighing you down? That’s the next step on our journey to overcoming worry.
Criticism is a part of life. Sometimes it’s fair, sometimes it’s not. The real trick isn’t avoiding criticism, but learning how to tell which feedback is actually useful. Imagine you’re working on a big project at your job. If someone gives you negative remarks, you have a choice: you can pick out the helpful advice and let the rest—like personal digs or off-base opinions—slide right off your shoulders.
But here’s something a lot of us struggle with: turning criticism inward and blaming ourselves more than we should. Have you ever found yourself replaying a mistake over and over, feeling like you just can’t let it go? That kind of self-accusation only ramps up anxiety, and honestly, it chips away at your confidence.
So, how do you actually manage criticism and let go of all that self-blame? Here are a few things to keep in mind:
First, listen to feedback with an open mind—but don’t be afraid to filter out what isn’t helpful or relevant.
Second, remember: nobody’s perfect. Mistakes happen, and each one is really just a chance to learn and grow.
And most importantly, practice self-compassion. Treat yourself with the same understanding and kindness you’d offer a good friend who’s struggling.
When you start to approach criticism this way, it loses its sting. You set your mind free from the heavy weight of constant self-judgment, making room for creativity, growth, and a much more peaceful outlook.
Up next, we’ll keep building on these ideas. We’ll look at how worry affects your physical health, why relaxation matters, and more practical strategies to help you live with less anxiety.
